title: Kraków in 3 days: Old Town, Wawel and the big day trips
author: Matt
intro: Three days is the right length for Kraków: one day for the Old Town and Wawel Castle, one for Auschwitz-Birkenau or the Wieliczka Salt Mine, and one for Kazimierz and the river. Here's how to fit it together.
seo_title: Kraków in 3 days: a day-by-day plan (2026)
seo_description: Day 1 Old Town and Wawel, day 2 Auschwitz or the salt mine, day 3 Kazimierz and Podgórze. A realistic 3-day Kraków plan with booking tips.

sections.heading: The short answer
sections.text:
- **Day 1:** Old Town and Wawel
- **Day 2:** Auschwitz or the salt mine
- **Day 3:** Kazimierz and Podgórze
- **Airport to centre:** about 18 mins by train

Kraków's centre is compact and flat, so you can walk almost everywhere. The day trips are what need planning, because the best slots book up, especially in summer. Book those first, then fit the city around them.

sections.heading: Three days at a glance
sections.text:
| Day | Morning | Afternoon | Evening |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | Main Market Square | Wawel Castle | Dinner in the Old Town |
| 2 | Auschwitz-Birkenau | Back to the city | A quiet evening in Kazimierz |
| 3 | Kazimierz | Schindler's Factory, Podgórze | Vistula riverside |

If you'd rather see the Wieliczka Salt Mine than Auschwitz, swap it into day 2. Trying to do both on one day is possible on a coach tour, but it's long and tiring.

sections.heading: Day 1: the Old Town and Wawel
sections.text:
Start on the **Main Market Square** (Rynek Główny), one of the largest medieval squares in Europe. In the middle is the Cloth Hall, a long Renaissance market hall still full of stalls. On the corner, **St Mary's Basilica** has a famous painted altarpiece, and every hour a trumpeter plays a tune from the taller tower that stops suddenly mid-note.

Walk down Grodzka street to **Wawel Hill**, with the royal castle and cathedral where Polish kings were crowned and buried. The state rooms and treasury are ticketed separately, so pick one or two rather than trying to see everything. At the foot of the hill, by the river, the **Wawel Dragon** statue breathes real fire every few minutes, a reliable hit with all ages.

Tip: the Planty, a ring of park where the city walls once stood, is the nicest way to walk between the sights.

sections.heading: Day 2: Auschwitz-Birkenau or the salt mine
sections.text:
**Auschwitz-Birkenau**, the former Nazi German concentration and extermination camp, is about 70 km west of Kraków in Oświęcim. Visiting is a sombre, unforgettable day. Since March 2026, all entry cards are only available online at visit.auschwitz.org. Entry is free, but unguided slots are limited, and a guided tour with a museum educator takes about three and a half hours. Booking opens up to 90 days ahead.

Watch out: free and guided slots sell out weeks ahead in summer. Book as soon as you've booked your flights, or join a tour from Kraków that includes transport and entry.

The **Wieliczka Salt Mine**, just south-east of the city, is a very different day out: underground chambers, lakes and a cathedral-sized chapel carved entirely from salt. You'll walk a long way and down a lot of steps, so wear comfy shoes, and allow about half a day including travel. Book a timed tour on the mine's official website.

sections.heading: Day 3: Kazimierz and Podgórze
sections.text:
**Kazimierz** was for centuries the centre of Jewish life in Kraków, and its synagogues, cemeteries and squares are worth a slow morning. Today it's also the city's liveliest area for cafés, bars and street food.

Cross the river to **Podgórze**, where the Nazis forced Kraków's Jews into a ghetto in 1941. The empty chairs on Ghetto Heroes Square are a simple memorial. Nearby, **Oskar Schindler's Enamel Factory** is now a museum about the city under occupation. Book a timed ticket in advance. End with a walk or drink along the Vistula, below Wawel, as the castle lights up.

sections.heading: Getting there and around
sections.text:
- **Flights:** Kraków has direct flights from many UK airports, taking about two and a half hours.
- **From the airport:** the train to Kraków Główny station takes about 18 minutes, and the station is a short walk from the Main Market Square.
- **Walking:** the Old Town, Wawel and Kazimierz are all within about 20 minutes on foot of each other.
- **Trams:** useful for Podgórze and the Schindler museum. Buy tickets from the machines or an app.
- **Money:** Poland uses the złoty, and cards are accepted almost everywhere.
- **Time:** Kraków is one hour ahead of the UK.

sections.heading: When to go
sections.text:
- **May to September:** warm and lively, with café tables out on the square.
- **December:** cold but festive, with a Christmas market in the Main Market Square. Our post on [Budapest or Kraków at Christmas](/blog/budapest-or-krakow-at-christmas) compares the two.
- **January and February:** very cold, often below freezing, but quiet and cheap.

Whatever the month, book Auschwitz and the salt mine first, then pick dates around them.

sections.heading: If you have longer
sections.text:
- **Go to the mountains:** [Zakopane](/destinations/zakopane), in the Tatras, is about two hours south by bus or train, with cable cars and hiking.
- **Add another city:** [Prague](/destinations/prague), [Vienna](/destinations/vienna) and [Budapest](/destinations/budapest) are all reachable by train, and we have three-day plans for [Prague](/blog/prague-in-3-days), [Vienna](/blog/vienna-in-3-days) and [Budapest](/blog/budapest-in-3-days).

sections.heading: Is Kraków the right city break?
sections.text:
Kraków is great value, compact and full of history, which makes it one of the best three-day breaks in Europe. Our list of the [best places for a 3-day city break](/blog/best-places-for-a-3-day-city-break-in-europe) compares it with other options, and the [Kraków guide](/destinations/krakow) has the best months and more ideas.

If you can't decide, browse the [city breaks](/destinations/city-breaks) page, or add a few cities to somewhere.party and let the draw choose.

faqs.question: Is 3 days enough for Kraków?
faqs.answer: Yes. Three days covers the Old Town, Wawel and Kazimierz, plus one big day trip to Auschwitz-Birkenau or the Wieliczka Salt Mine. Add a fourth day for both day trips or Zakopane.

faqs.question: Do you need to book Auschwitz in advance?
faqs.answer: Yes. Since March 2026, entry cards are only available online at visit.auschwitz.org, and slots sell out weeks ahead in summer.

faqs.question: Can you do Auschwitz and the Wieliczka Salt Mine in one day?
faqs.answer: Some tours combine them, but it makes a very long day. Most people find it better to spread them over two days.

faqs.question: How do you get from Kraków Airport to the city centre?
faqs.answer: The train takes about 18 minutes to Kraków Główny station, which is a short walk from the Old Town.
